clinician.trajectory_summary: The patient presented with viral prodromal symptoms, fever, and respiratory findings including patchy infiltrates on CXR. On day 7, he developed acute neurological deficits characterized by disorientation, rambling speech, right-sided facial droop, and upper and lower extremity flaccidity. An initial CT head ruled out acute intracranial hemorrhage. Subsequent CTA revealed multiple large vessel occlusions, specifically complete occlusion at the origin of the LICA and proximal RVA, along with severe stenosis of the proximal RICA. A repeat CT confirmed an acute multilobar infarct in the left frontal, parietal, and insular cortex. The patient's clinical course also included worsening respiratory failure requiring intubation.

A repeat CT revealed hypodensities within the left frontal and parietal lobes affecting the surrounding insular cortex, suggesting an acute multilobar infarct over distributions of the left anterior and MCA.
Patient developed worsening respiratory failure requiring intubation and transfer to ICU.
